---
title: "05 · Practice — Group Actions"
---

Do the three solved exercises first: each one isolates a way symmetry counting
goes wrong — uneven orbit sizes, prescribed multiplicities, and division by a
non-unit. The contest problems then build from a single rotation group up to
Burnside over all of $S_n$.

## Solved exercises

### A. A weight that cannot be divided uniformly

List binary necklaces of length three. Why is $2^3/3$ meaningless as a count?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Separate constant strings from strings with one minority color.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
Representatives are 000, 001, 011, 111, with orbit sizes 1, 3, 3, 1.
Their sizes sum to 8, but there is no common orbit size to divide by.
Burnside gives $(8+2+2)/3=4$.
:::

### B. Two red beads on a square

Count square bead colorings with exactly two red and two blue beads up to
rotation. Then add reflection symmetry.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The half-turn fixes two such colorings; quarter-turns fix none.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
The identity fixes $\binom42=6$. Rotation Burnside gives $(6+2)/4=2$.
Representatives have adjacent or opposite red beads. Both are preserved as
classes under reflection, so the bracelet count is also two. Counting all
$2^{z(g)}$ fixed colorings would ignore the prescribed multiplicities.
:::

### C. Integer division after modular reduction

A group of size six has Burnside numerator 42. Recover its orbit count modulo
four without inverting six. Generalize the method.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Preserve the numerator modulo the product of the divisor and target modulus.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
$42\bmod24=18$, and $18/6=3\equiv7\pmod4$. In general retain the numerator
modulo $gm$ then divide its representative by $g$. Keeping only modulo $m$
loses information: residues 2 could represent numerator 6 or 18, whose
quotients differ modulo 4.
:::

## 1. UVA 10294 — Arif in Dhaka (First Love Part 2) (`Foundation`)

- [Statement mirror](https://onlinejudge.org/external/102/10294.pdf) · English
- [CP-Algorithms derivation](https://cp-algorithms.com/combinatorics/burnside.html)
- Train: derive cyclic and dihedral cycle structures from first principles.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Average fixed colorings over rotations for necklaces and over rotations plus reflections for bracelets.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>A rotation by $r$ fixes $t^{\gcd(n,r)}$ strings.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Split reflection contributions by parity of $n$.</details>

## 2. AtCoder ABC 198 F — Cube (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc198/tasks/abc198_f) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc198/editorial/1080) · English/Japanese
- Train: enumerate the 24 rotations of a cube by cycle type and count
  positive integer assignments with a prescribed weighted sum.
- Later prerequisite: [rational generating functions](../10-generating-functions/chapter.qmd)
  or [recurrence evaluation](../07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd) for the large total weight.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Burnside acts on the six faces, not the eight vertices.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Classify rotations by axis: face, edge, or opposite vertices.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>For cycle lengths $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$, a fixed labelling contributes $[x^S]\prod_j x^{\ell_j}/(1-x^{\ell_j})$: one positive value is repeated around each cycle.</details>

## 3. CSES 2210 — Counting Grids (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://cses.fi/problemset/task/2210/) ·
  [Burnside tutorial and problem list](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/102668) · English
- Train: enumerate the rotation group of a square grid and count position cycles.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>The group has the identity and rotations by 90, 180, and 270 degrees.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>A fixed binary grid is constant on every orbit of cells under that rotation.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Derive the orbit counts separately for odd and even side lengths.</details>

## 4. AtCoder ABC 284 Ex — Count Unlabeled Graphs (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc284/tasks/abc284_h) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc284/editorial/5481) · Japanese
- Train: Burnside over the symmetric group, conjugacy classes, induced
  permutations on unordered vertex pairs, and surjective vertex colorings.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Model an object as a surjective $K$-coloring of labelled vertices together with an edge subset; then take its orbit under vertex permutations.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Sum by cycle type (integer partition), not over all $N!$ permutations.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>A fixed coloring is constant on vertex cycles, while an invariant edge set is constant on induced pair cycles. Count both, and enforce use of every color inside the fixed-point count.</details>
